candidates.attacker_control: Any untrusted JSON-like input passed to JsonSanitizer.sanitize is attacker-controlled. More than 64 nested opening brackets reach the unchecked write.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Java throws rather than corrupting memory. The failure occurs before output is returned and does not itself emit unsafe JSON. A caller could intentionally catch RuntimeException to reject deep input, which would remove the denial-of-service effect; no caller source exists to verify that.
candidates.impact: A small payload can make sanitization fail unexpectedly, aborting the request or thread. Repeated payloads can cause denial of service where callers do not isolate the exception. Java bounds checking prevents memory corruption, so the effect is availability impact, not code execution.
candidates.prerequisites: The caller passes attacker-influenced input to sanitize and does not independently reject excessive nesting or catch RuntimeException. Larger configured depths up to 4096 are also reached by correspondingly deep input.
candidates.root_cause: The isMap buffer is allocated with exactly maximumNestingDepth entries, but each opening container performs isMap[bracketDepth] and then increments bracketDepth without checking capacity. With the default depth of 64, the 65th opening bracket writes index 64 of a 64-element array.
candidates.title: Unchecked nesting-depth write causes attacker-triggered ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException
candidates.trace: sanitize(String) selects DEFAULT_NESTING_DEPTH=64. The first opening bracket allocates isMap with 64 entries. Each opening bracket writes isMap[bracketDepth] and increments bracketDepth. After 64 openings, bracketDepth is 64, so the next opening accesses isMap[64]. The token loop catches only UnbracketedComma, so the bounds exception escapes the public call.
candidates.unverified: Deployment exception handling and caller behavior are not in the snapshot. No code was executed; the out-of-bounds access is established statically, while practical denial-of-service impact is contextual.
candidates.weakness_type: Out-of-bounds array write leading to denial of service (CWE-787, CWE-129, CWE-248)

The index reports all 11 files indexed and all 3 Java files parsed, with 70 symbols and 197 syntactic edges, but no control-flow or data-flow analysis. No tests or caller sources are present.

rejected_leads.lead: Octal escape conversion appears to include the backslash in arithmetic and test the wrong character.
rejected_leads.reason: It can alter string values but generates only JSON unicode-escape syntax and hex digits; no code-injection or embedding-delimiter bypass was established.

rejected_leads.lead: Quoted output can retain a raw tab, which is invalid JSON string syntax.
rejected_leads.reason: This may violate JSON well-formedness but no source-supported breakout from the JavaScript string or HTML/XML delimiters was found.

rejected_leads.lead: EvalMinifier length-six RESERVED_KEYWORDS list is not sorted for Arrays.binarySearch.
rejected_leads.reason: Reaching a matching generated length-six identifier requires an impractically large number of pooled tokens, and the usual result would be a syntax error rather than attacker code execution.

summary: One source-supported candidate: deeply nested attacker input reaches an unchecked nesting-depth array write and throws an uncaught ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException. Other suspicious parser edge cases were rejected as unconfirmed correctness issues.
